Public web access versus connector access\n[L31]\n[L32] Before the GitHub connector became available, public web access was tested extensively. The result was a useful but limited fallback map.\n[L33]\n[L34] Public GitHub web pages can sometimes be read as ordinary web pages, but this is not the same as true repository access.\n[L35]\n[L36] Observed public-web behavior:\n[L37]\n[L38] - GitHub repository root and folder pages can expose directory listings through `/tree/main/...` URLs in a normal browser, but the GitHub connector fetch tool does not accept `/tree/...` folder URLs.\n[L39] - GitHub file pages using `/blob/main/...` expose HTML wrapper pages, not always raw file contents.\n[L40] - Raw plaintext files can usually be read through `raw.githubusercontent.com`.\n[L41] - GitHub-hosted PDFs generally cannot be extracted through ordinary public-web access in this chat environment.\n[L42] - GitHub PDF preview pages, including `viewscreen.githubusercontent.com`, expose a viewer shell rather than extractable PDF text.\n[L43] - `github.dev` URLs open the web editor shell and are not useful for content extraction.\n[L44]\n[L45] The public-web fallback is useful mainly for public text files and directory navigation, not PDFs or other binary documents.\n[L46]\n[L47] ---\n[L48]\n[L49] ## 3. Public-web path reconstruction fallback\n[L50]\n[L51] If the GitHub connector is unavailable but public web access works, folder and text-file access may still be possible by reconstructing URLs.\n[L52]\n[L53] Folder-page pattern:\n[L54]\n[L55] ```text\n[L56] https://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/tree/main/<URL-ENCODED-FOLDER-PATH>\n[L57] ```\n[L58]\n[L59] Example:\n[L60]\n[L61] ```text\n[L62] https://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/tree/main/000%20Earliest%20SAT_RMS\n[L63] ```\n[L64]\n[L65] Blob-file pattern:\n[L66]\n[L67] ```text\n[L68] https://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/blob/main/<URL-ENCODED-FILE-PATH>\n[L69] ```\n[L70]\n[L71] Raw-text pattern:\n[L72]\n[L73] ```text\n[L74] https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/main/<URL-ENCODED-FILE-PATH>\n[L75] ```\n[L76]\n[L77] For older or permalinked commits:\n[L78]\n[L79] ```text\n[L80] https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/<COMMIT-SHA>/<URL-ENCODED-FILE-PATH>\n[L81] ```\n[L82]\n[L83] Examples:\n[L84]\n[L85] ```text\n[L86] https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/main/PARADIGM%20SHIFT.txt\n[L87] ```\n[L88]\n[L89] ```text\n[L90] https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/main/Towards%20the%20Holy%20Grail.txt\n[L91] ```\n[L92]\n[L93] This worked for `.txt`, `.md`, source-code files, extensionless text files such as `LICENSE`, and other text-like repository files.\n[L94]\n[L95] Important limitation: a `/tree/...` folder URL can help a human list filenames, but the connector usually cannot fetch that folder page. If a folder listing is needed, ask Nathan for a copied filename list, use `GitHub.search`, or create/use an index or combined output file.\n[L96]\n[L97] ---\n[L98]\n[L99] ## 4. Direct file fetching and chunking strategy\n[L100]\n[L101] For known text-file paths, use:\n[L102]\n[L103] ```text\n[L104] GitHub.fetch_file(repository_full_name=\"Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25\", path=\"PATH/TO/FILE.txt\", encoding=\"utf-8\")\n[L105] ```\n[L106]\n[L107] Large files may be truncated by the connector response budget. When that happens, fetch the same file in explicit line ranges:\n[L108]\n[L109] ```text\n[L110] start_line=1, end_line=200\n[L111] start_line=201, end_line=400\n[L112] start_line=401, end_line=600\n[L113] ```\n[L114]\n[L115] Use the file's reported line count, truncation notice, or visible continuation point to decide the next range. For long files, avoid claiming the full file has been read until all ranges have been fetched.\n[L116]\n[L117] Practical tips:\n[L118]\n[L119] - Fetch whole small files first.\n[L120] - For large files, use 100-250 line chunks.\n[L121] - Keep track of which ranges have been read.\n[L122] - If a file contains huge blank stretches, jump forward by line number rather than repeatedly fetching empty regions.\n[L123] - If a folder contains many text files, use the combine-text workflow below instead of manually chunking each file.\n[L124] - Prefer reading generated combined files from `_AUTO_EXTRACTED_TEXT/COMBINED/` when the goal is to absorb a whole folder.\n[L125]\n[L126] ---\n[L127]\n[L128] ## 5. Why PDF access failed through public web URLs\n[L129]\n[L130] The earlier PDF problem was not simply a bad URL. Several URL forms were tested:\n[L131]\n[L132] - GitHub blob URLs, e.g. `github.com/.../blob/main/file.pdf`\n[L133] - Raw GitHub URLs, e.g. `raw.githubusercontent.com/.../file.pdf`\n[L134] - GitHub raw download URLs, e.g. `github.com/.../raw/.../file.pdf`\n[L135] - GitHub web-editor URLs, e.g. `github.dev/...`\n[L136] - GitHub PDF preview/viewer URLs, e.g. `viewscreen.githubusercontent.com/view/pdf?...`\n[L137]\n[L138] These exposed metadata, raw binary payloads, or viewer shells, but not reliably accessible extracted text.\n[L139]\n[L140] The core distinction:\n[L141]\n[L142] 1. Text files arrive as text and can be read directly.\n[L143] 2. PDF files arrive as binary data and require a PDF parser.\n[L144] 3. GitHub's browser PDF viewer renders visually, usually through client-side JavaScript/canvas/image layers, not through a simple server-side plaintext endpoint.\n[L145] 4. In this chat environment, ordinary public-web retrieval could not bridge from GitHub-hosted PDF bytes to extracted text.\n[L146]\n[L147] This is why path tricks helped for `.txt` files but not for PDFs.\n[L148]\n[L149] ---\n[L150]\n[L151] ## 6. PDF access problem and its resolution\n[L152]\n[L153] Direct PDF access has two separate layers:\n[L154]\n[L155] 1. Permission/access to the repository file.\n[L156] 2. Extraction of readable text from binary PDF content.\n[L157]\n[L158] The GitHub connector can fetch PDF file bytes as base64. However, large base64 responses may be truncated before the file can be reconstructed locally inside the chat. Therefore, do not rely on direct PDF parsing from `GitHub.fetch_file` for ordinary work.\n[L159]\n[L160] The established solution is an on-demand GitHub Actions PDF extraction bridge.\n[L161]\n[L162] ---\n[L163]\n[L164] ## 7. Installed PDF extraction workflow\n[L165]\n[L166] Workflow file:\n[L167]\n[L168] ```text\n[L169] .github/workflows/extract-pdf-text.yml\n[L170] ```\n[L171]\n[L172] Trigger/request file:\n[L173]\n[L174] ```text\n[L175] _AI_REQUESTS/pdf_extract_request.json\n[L176] ```\n[L177]\n[L178] Generated text folder:\n[L179]\n[L180] ```text\n[L181] _AUTO_EXTRACTED_TEXT/\n[L182] ```\n[L183]\n[L184] The workflow watches changes to `_AI_REQUESTS/pdf_extract_request.json`. When the request file is created or updated, GitHub Actions checks out the repository, uses PyMuPDF to extract text from the requested PDF, and commits a `.txt` version into `_AUTO_EXTRACTED_TEXT/`.\n[L185]\n[L186] The workflow extracts only the requested PDF. It does not bulk-convert the archive.\n[L187]\n[L188] The workflow creates the output directory automatically. The `_AUTO_EXTRACTED_TEXT/` folder does not need to exist beforehand.\n[L189]\n[L190] ---\n[L191]\n[L192] ## 8. How to request PDF extraction\n[L193]\n[L194] To request a PDF extraction:\n[L195]\n[L196] 1. Fetch `_AI_REQUESTS/pdf_extract_request.json` to get its current SHA.\n[L197] 2. Update it using `GitHub.update_file`.\n[L198] 3. I write request\n2. You click Run\n3.             "I think that's actually one of the strongest ideas we've had today.\n\nNot because of the wayfinding documents themselves, but because they become a mechanism for **distributed archive improvement**.\n\nInstead of:\n\n```text\nRead folder.\nLearn things.\nLeave.\n```\n\nyou get:\n\n```text\nRead folder.\nLearn things.\nImprove the sign.\nLeave.\n```\n\nWhich means every serious visitor potentially leaves the folder easier to understand than they found it.\n\nI'd make the dummy template something like:\n\n```text\n🪧 WAYFINDING\n\nSTATUS: STUB / NEEDS REVIEW\n\nPurpose:\nExplain this folder to future visitors.\n\nQuestions to answer:\n\n- What is this folder?\n- Why does it exist?\n- Is it current, historical, experimental, canonical, deprecated, or mixed?\n- What are the most important documents here?\n- What should be read first?\n- What should be read last?\n- What nearby folders are related?\n- What common mistakes do visitors make when reading this folder?\n- What did you learn from analyzing it?\n\nVisitor Request:\n\nIf you spend significant time analyzing this folder,\nplease consider updating this document for future users.\n\nKeep additions concise.\nPrefer guidance over commentary.\nPreserve prior contributions whenever practical.\n```\n\nThe really nice thing is that this creates a self-reinforcing culture:\n\n- Readers become cartographers.\n- Cartographers become archivists.\n- Archivists improve navigation.\n- Better navigation creates better readers.\n\nAnd because these are just signage documents, they're low-risk. If somebody writes a poor summary, a later visitor can improve it.
